agency: Vermont Agency of Human Services (AHS), Department for Children and Families (DCF), Economic Services Division (ESD)
admin_note: Vermont is a STATE-ADMINISTERED SNAP program — DCF's Economic Services Division (ESD) administers directly through district offices with no county-level policy variation, structurally similar to this roster's Delaware, Nebraska, Connecticut, North Carolina, Ohio, New Jersey, Tennessee, Indiana, Missouri, Maryland, Colorado, South Carolina, Alabama, Louisiana, Kentucky, Oklahoma, Utah, Iowa, Arkansas, Mississippi, Kansas, New Mexico, and New Hampshire packs. GENUINE STRUCTURAL FLAGSHIP FINDING: Vermont runs a second, DISTINCT categorical-eligibility gate beyond the standard 185% FPL Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE) gross-income test that most secondary sources describe: households WITH CHILDREN that received the Vermont Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) in the 12 months before applying are categorically eligible for 3SquaresVT and do not have to pass either the gross or net income test at all — a state-EITC-linked categorical-eligibility mechanism this pack found distinct from (and narrower/differently-triggered than) Delaware's TANF-funded-pregnancy-prevention-service mechanism, though both serve the same structural purpose of exempting large swaths of working households from a resource test. SECOND FLAGSHIP FINDING, a genuine correction of an incomplete flat 'no Restaurant Meals Program' framing several secondary sources use: Vermont does NOT operate a formal SNAP Restaurant Meals Program (RMP) — DCF's own February 2025 legislative report confirms Vermont opposed 2024's S.215, which would have required RMP implementation — but Vermont is one of only five states nationally with authority to issue SNAP benefits as unrestricted CASH (not EBT) to households where every member is 65+ and/or receiving SSI; per that same DCF report, 43% of Vermont's 3SquaresVT caseload (16,823 of 39,112 households) currently receives benefits this way, and cash-out households can and do spend those benefits at restaurants or on hot/prepared foods exactly like ordinary income, despite Vermont having no formal RMP program at all. THIRD FINDING (legacy-manual-mirror trap, confirmed not a fetch-tooling artifact): the widely-linked 'Code of Vermont Rules' 3SquaresVT mirror hosted on Cornell Law School's Legal Information Institute (regulations.justia.com's identical text is Cloudflare-gated) serves a clean HTTP 200 with well-formatted, official-looking regulatory text, but that text is a stale, largely-unmaintained reprint of the generic pre-2010s 7 CFR 273 federal base rule — it cites 'the Food Stamp Act of 1977,' shows internal effective-date markers like 'November 1, 1998,' and contains NO trace of Vermont's own distinctive 185% FPL BBCE gate, EITC categorical-eligibility mechanism, cash-out option, current OBBBA-era ABAWD exemption criteria, or any dollar figure newer than a base $3,000 general resource limit. This pack treats DCF's live, actively-maintained consumer pages (dcf.vermont.gov) and DCF's own dated legislative testimony/slide decks as authoritative over this legacy CVR mirror wherever they diverge, and flags the mirror's staleness explicitly rather than citing it as a live source of Vermont-specific figures.
system: DCF's Economic Services Division (ESD) processes 3SquaresVT centrally (no county offices with independent policy authority); applicants apply online through the myBenefits portal (also used for Reach Up, Essential Person, and Fuel Assistance), by mailing or dropping off a paper Form 202 (or Form 202-3SNP for the age-60+/disabled simplified process) at a district office, or via ESD's secure document uploader. Vermont's standard certification period is 12 months for most households (interim report due in month 5), extending to 24-36 months (up to a full 3 years with no interim report) for households using the '3SquaresVT in a SNAP' simplified process, available when everyone applying is 60+ or receiving disability benefits, earns no job/self-employment income, and buys/prepares food together. Vermont's own regulatory-code mirror is flagged in this pack as lagging currently-operative DCF policy in multiple specific, confirmed places — see freshness.json.

verification.method: dcf.vermont.gov, legislature.vermont.gov, and law.cornell.edu all returned clean HTTP 200 to direct curl attempts with a standard browser User-Agent — no persistent WAF/bot-detection barrier of the kind this roster's New Hampshire and Maine packs encountered, though a single dcf.vermont.gov fetch attempt returned a transient HTTP 403 that succeeded cleanly on an immediate retry (not treated as a genuine barrier). regulations.justia.com, hosting an identical copy of the same Code of Vermont Rules text as the Cornell LII mirror, returned a hard Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' challenge page to both a direct curl attempt and an r.jina.ai reader-proxy retry; this pack worked around it by using the Cornell LII mirror instead, which serves the same underlying regulatory text without a bot-detection wall. The genuinely operative regulatory-manual host this pack could NOT productively access is the 3SquaresVT Program Manual hosted on ahsnet.ahs.state.vt.us (a MadCap/RoboHelp client-side JavaScript application, similar in kind to Delaware's regulations.delaware.gov SPA problem but WITHOUT a discoverable underlying API/PDF endpoint this pack could locate — the index.htm shell fetched cleanly at HTTP 200 but rendered no server-side content, and this pack's attempts to guess the RoboHelp Data/Toc.js and search-index asset paths all 404'd); WebSearch results independently describe this same manual host as restricted to 'AHS employees and authorized users' for at least some pages, which is consistent with this pack's inability to retrieve rendered content from it. This pack treated DCF's own live, actively-maintained public consumer pages and DCF's own dated legislative testimony/slide decks (which are official primary-source documents authored by DCF's Deputy Commissioner and Program Director, submitted to the Vermont Legislature) as authoritative in place of the inaccessible internal program manual, and separately flags the Cornell LII 'Code of Vermont Rules' mirror as a confirmed STALE legacy reprint (see admin_note) rather than as a source of current Vermont-specific figures.
verification.gates: regulations.justia.com returned a hard Cloudflare bot-detection challenge ('Just a moment... Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue') to both a direct curl attempt with a browser User-Agent and an r.jina.ai reader-proxy retry — this pack worked around it by using law.cornell.edu's identical mirror of the same Code of Vermont Rules text instead, which served cleanly. ahsnet.ahs.state.vt.us (the 3SquaresVT Program Manual, DCF's own primary regulatory manual) is a client-side JavaScript RoboHelp/MadCap application with no server-rendered content; this pack's attempts to locate the underlying content/search-index API endpoints (by analogy to Delaware's successful regulations.delaware.gov API-endpoint workaround) all returned HTTP 404, and WebSearch results independently suggest at least some of this host's content is restricted to authorized AHS users — this pack treats this as a genuine, disclosed access gap rather than fabricating manual section citations, and relies on DCF's live consumer pages plus DCF's own dated legislative testimony as the operative substitute. A single dcf.vermont.gov/esd/laws-rules/procedures fetch attempt returned a transient HTTP 403 that succeeded cleanly on an immediate retry with no User-Agent change — likely simple rate-limiting rather than a persistent WAF wall, since every other dcf.vermont.gov page fetched cleanly on the first attempt.
